title: Eiffel Tower 3D
tagline: A quiet 1889 museum exhibit in your browser: a 12-stop camera tour, archival photos, English and French.

steps.title: At a glance
steps.goal: Decide in two minutes: **is this what I want built?** Nothing is built yet; this is the proposal.

blocks.md: A calm, grey-toned **3D exhibit of Gustave Eiffel's tower as it stood in 1889**, drawn live in the browser from code (no model files, no account, no server, no AI). A visitor presses **Explore** and the camera glides through **12 stops**: Eiffel's design drawing, the foundations, the rising ironwork, the finished tower. Eleven stops pair the 3D view with an archival photograph; the last stop is the whole tower to turn around yourself. One button switches every caption between English and French.

items.v: Visitors who want a quiet, museum-style visit; also a good test of smooth, jump-free camera work
Any modern desktop or phone browser with 3D (WebGL); works offline after the first load
No backend, login, analytics, AI, audio or VR
Three small decisions, each with a safe default (step 7)

steps.title: Drags with mouse or finger

  V->>UI: press Explore or Next

steps.title: Decisions and risks
steps.goal: Three questions are still **open**. Each has a default, so silence means the default.

items.default: none: no key, no model calls, no network after install
items.ifNo: adds a key, a server and cost

items.default: three.js r186, installed (not copied, not from a CDN)
items.ifNo: none of the visuals; only how it ships

items.default: simple lattice (boxes and tubes), 4 piers, 3 platforms
items.ifNo: a finer 13-part model is possible but is a large extra phase

items.default: ground, lawn, a few low blocks, fog; if that is too heavy: ground and sky only (we will say so)
items.ifNo: a richer city means more work and a slower page

items.default: camera pose and field of view from the data table; if it does not line up: the photo card shows without alignment (we will say so)

steps.title: How we will know it is done
steps.goal: Tick these as you check them. **"Looks good" is not a check**; each one is a click path or a number.

items: **No errors:** the page console stays at 0 errors across the whole tour in both languages.
**Look:** neutral grey only; caption contrast at least 4.5:1; every button at least 40 x 40 px; no text under 11 px.
**Speed:** 60 fps on a laptop is the target and 30 the floor while touring (guessed, measured and reported).
**Phone:** usable at 390 px wide, no sideways scroll.
**Motion:** with reduced motion on, nothing loops forever and moves become instant.
**Nothing self-glowing:** a built-in audit reports 0 offenders.
**Honest report:** the builders list every difference from this plan and every check they could not run.
